title: Questions, question tags, indirect questions
subtitle: Word order in questions, tags, and polite indirect questions

rows.example: **Do** you feel cold? **Did** they go shopping?
**Am** I annoying you? **Were** they waiting for you?
**Have** you seen this film? **Had** it started?
**Am** I late? **Were** you all right? **Have** you been ill?
**Does** she **have** a bath every day? **Did** they **have** lunch at one o'clock?
**Should** I call the police? **Could** you call me later?
**Who** was in prison? **What's** your name? **Where** do they live? **Why** did you do that?

blocks.text: To form questions in the passive, we put the auxiliary verb before the subject. If there is more than one auxiliary verb, only the first one goes before the subject.

blocks.intro: With the question words **who** and **what**, we use **do** as an auxiliary verb if the question word refers to the object of the verb.
items: **Who told you?** (= Someone told you. Who?)
**Who did you tell?** (= You told someone. Who?)

rows.use: To ask someone to agree with us
To check whether something is true
rows.example: You haven't been to prison, **have you**?
Phil works here, **doesn't he**? They didn't leave, **did they**?
You are coming, **aren't you**? They weren't looking, **were they**?
They've gone, **haven't they**? You hadn't seen it, **had you**?
He's new here, **isn't he**? You weren't old enough, **were you**?
They have a car, **haven't / don't they**? You didn't have a shower every day, **did you**?
Jan **should** be here by now, **shouldn't he**? You **won't** make a mess, **will you**?

items: In sentences with **I am**, we use **aren't I**? In sentences with **I'm not**, we use **am I**?
I'm right, **aren't I**? I'm not stupid, **am I**?

blocks.text: With **Let's**, we use **shall** in the question tag.
blocks.note: Let's do the washing-up later, **shall we**?

blocks.text: We use a phrase + a clause with normal word order to ask questions politely.

rows.example: **Can/Could you tell me** where the bank is? **Do you know** if Alison lives there? **I wonder if** Alison could tell me where the toilets are.

blocks.text: We don't use question word order in the second half of the sentence.
blocks.note: I wonder if you know how much this costs. (not **how much does this cost**)

exercises.title: A · Correct the question
exercises.instruction: The words and phrases in bold in each sentence are wrong. Write the correct word or phrase.

items.prompt: Does Debbie **likes** Greek food?
Did Anne and Carlo **went** to Spain last year?
acceptedAnswers: Did Anne and Carlo go to Spain last year?
Did Anne and Carlo go to Spain last year

items.prompt: **Was** Dawn and Jennifer with you?
acceptedAnswers: Were Dawn and Jennifer with you?
Were Dawn and Jennifer with you

items.prompt: Has Claudia **a haircut** every Thursday?
acceptedAnswers: Does Claudia have a haircut every Thursday?
Does Claudia have a haircut every Thursday

items.prompt: Have you **buy** the new Arctic Monkeys' CD yet?
acceptedAnswers: Have you bought the new Arctic Monkeys' CD yet?
Have you bought the new Arctic Monkeys' CD yet

items.prompt: **Does** Tim going to be in the school play?
acceptedAnswers: Is Tim going to be in the school play?
Is Tim going to be in the school play

items.prompt: It **would be** the best thing to do?
acceptedAnswers: Would it be the best thing to do?
Would it be the best thing to do

items.prompt: Were you **play** basketball when it started snowing?
acceptedAnswers: Were you playing basketball when it started snowing?
Were you playing basketball when it started snowing

exercises.title: B · Dialogue
exercises.instruction: Write one word in each gap.

items.prompt: Rachel: Hi, Ben! (1) ___ are you?
Ben: I'm fine. (2) ___ you hear about Mr Watkins, the maths teacher?
Rachel: No. (3) ___ happened to him?

Ben: He fell out of the window of his classroom!
Rachel: (4) ___ pushed him?

Ben: No one!
Rachel: So how (5) ___ it happen?

Ben: He was sitting on the windowsill and he just fell backwards!
Rachel: Oh dear! Poor Mr Watkins. (6) ___ he hurt?

Ben: No. Luckily his classroom is on the ground floor.
Rachel: That's lucky! (7) ___ you there at the time?

Ben: Yes! We were having a maths lesson.
Rachel: So (8) ___ did you all do?

Ben: We ran outside to help him. We were all laughing, though!
Rachel: (9) ___ he think it was funny, too?
